title: ACR credential lifecycle event (v1 wire format)
description:
One lifecycle event of an ACR client credential (fcacr_), as the Auth Control Plane receives it. ACR owns the credential: it generates the plaintext, keeps the hashed lookup and validates the data plane (ACP-ADR-08). The Auth Control Plane receives only this metadata projection, so the event is a closed description of lifecycle state and can carry no secret, verifier, token, token prefix or fingerprint: every member of the envelope, the payload and each change object is named here, additionalProperties is false at every level, and a test walks this schema and fails on any member name that suggests secret material.

THE IDEMPOTENCY KEY IS (aggregate_type, aggregate_id, revision), and `revision` is PER AGGREGATE (the aggregate is one credential, aggregate_id is the acr credential id, the registry's external_reference), never global. The `idempotency_key` must equal aggregate_type + ":" + aggregate_id + ":" + payload.revision, which the clients enforce. Consumer rule, the same as provisioning-event.v1: apply an event when its revision is exactly the last applied revision + 1 (or 1 for a credential never seen); a revision at or below the last applied one is a duplicate or stale delivery and is ignored; a larger one is a gap, which is not applied and means the consumer must resynchronise.

LIFECYCLE. `issued`, `device_redeemed` and `rotated` open an aggregate and are revision 1. `device_redeemed` is a credential issued by redeeming a device authorization (acr class native_device or oauth_user). A rotation issues a NEW credential (its own aggregate) whose `rotated` event names the credential it replaces in `rotation_parent_id`. With no overlap acr also writes `revoked` for the replaced credential in the same transaction; with an overlap the replaced credential stays active and receives `expired` when its cut expires_at passes. `revoked` and `expired` are later events (revision 2 or more) and are terminal. A browser credential is never rotated. Scopes never change after issue: this contract has no scope or audience event, and a rotation never widens its parent, which the projection core enforces because a schema cannot compare two events.

ACTOR. `actor_type` (user, operator, credential, system) is acr's audit actor type. `actor_ref` names the actor, opaque to the Auth Control Plane, and is required unless the actor is the system, which has none. A credential acting on itself is actor_type credential: on `revoked` its actor_ref equals aggregate_id and on `rotated` it equals rotation_parent_id, which the clients enforce. `expired` is always written by the system.

`revision` is an integer token in 1..2^53-1; a decimal- or exponent-form token is refused by the clients on the raw token.

aggregate_id.description: The credential's id in the ACR domain (the registry's external_reference).

idempotency_key.description: Must equal aggregate_type:aggregate_id:payload.revision; the schema pins the shape and the clients enforce the equality (reject_by_client).

created_at.description: When the mutation committed. RFC 3339, every component bounded as in error.v1.

organization_id.description: The tenant the credential belongs to, in the Auth Control Plane's form.

actor_ref.description: The actor's acr-side id. Required unless actor_type is system, refused for system.

acr_class.description: The issuance class acr derived for the credential (acr client_class). A closed vocabulary of six.

owner_subject.description: The acr-side owner or approving subject, opaque to the Auth Control Plane. Absent for org_bearer, operator and workload credentials.

acr_class.description: The issuance class acr derived for the credential (acr client_class). A closed vocabulary of six.

owner_subject.description: The acr-side owner or approving subject, opaque to the Auth Control Plane. Absent for org_bearer, operator and workload credentials.

acr_class.description: The issuance class acr derived for the credential (acr client_class). A closed vocabulary of six.

owner_subject.description: The acr-side owner or approving subject, opaque to the Auth Control Plane. Absent for org_bearer, operator and workload credentials.

timestamp.description: RFC 3339, every component bounded as in error.v1.

opaqueId.description: An opaque identifier of the acr domain: letters, digits, underscore, hyphen.

scopes.description: Scope names, the shape credential_registry.scopes and principal.v1 carry. A set, at most 64. Never empty: a credential with no scope is not issued.
